# Registry Stack

> Open-source software for organizations that maintain registries and the services that rely on them. Base Registry Engine stores and manages records about people, households, organizations, assets, and more. It supports record creation, retrieval, relationships, controlled updates, and history, with review where required. Evidence Gateway lets approved services receive signed answers about defined facts without receiving the full source record. Each product works independently. Registry Casework assigns review requests to staff, tracks due dates, and records the decision; it returns that decision to the service that asked, which applies any change under its own rules.

Organizations own their records and define the rules for access and changes. The software is Apache-2.0 open source. Paid implementation pilots and annual support contracts are available for teams that need help, separate from self-service use. Current starting prices and scope are on the pricing page.

## Website

- [Home](https://registrystack.org/): Registry maintenance and fact-sharing examples, the kinds of register the software serves, product choices, and next steps.
- [Solutions](https://registrystack.org/solutions/): Organized by the register an organization keeps: licensing and professional registers; business, tax and finance; people, households and social programmes; land, property, vehicles and places; agriculture, animals, food and environment; health, safety and regulated products; public bodies, reference lists and catalogues. Two further pages cover checking a fact between services and reviewing changes that need a person.
- [Starters](https://registrystack.org/starters/): Starting configurations for common registers, grouped by register family. A starter is a starting point to adapt, not a deployment.
- [Starter pages](https://registrystack.org/starters/): Each starter has its own page at https://registrystack.org/starters/<id>/ listing its record types, staff actions, access profiles, included parts, and the public registers it was modelled on. Starters are free and available on request: each page has a request-access form with an email fallback. They are not a public download.
- [Base Registry Engine](https://registrystack.org/products/base-registry/): Build and run the base registry other services rely on, with defined records and relationships, storage, access controls, and change history behind the organization's applications.
- [Evidence Gateway](https://registrystack.org/products/evidence-gateway/): Return signed answers from an existing registry or another configured source.
- [Registry Casework](https://registrystack.org/products/casework/): Staff review of requests that need a person to decide: queues, the officer responsible, due dates, and recorded decisions. Requests can come from a register, a case system, or another service. Registry Casework returns the decision to the service that asked and does not change the register itself. Connecting a register other than Base Registry Engine requires integration work.
- [Blog](https://registrystack.org/blog/): Field guides for registry owners and reviewers, such as defining the question before connecting a registry and reconstructing who accessed what. RSS at https://registrystack.org/rss.xml.
- [Local government](https://registrystack.org/solutions/local-government/): Local permit and registration services, from applications and staff review to record updates, notices and renewals.
- [Verifiable credentials](https://registrystack.org/solutions/verifiable-credentials/): Digital credentials that state information from a register, such as a licence's recorded status, signed so a receiving service can check who issued them and whether they were altered.
- [Digital public infrastructure](https://registrystack.org/digital-public-infrastructure/): Reusable registry capabilities for digital public infrastructure, with open-source software, documented interfaces and institutional control.
- [AI-assisted customization](https://registrystack.org/customization/): The Registry Stack team uses AI-assisted authoring to adapt configuration and application code; the institution reviews the result before deployment. Running the service does not require an AI model.
- [Implementation and support](https://registrystack.org/pricing/): Implementation pilots, annual support contracts, and a written inquiry covering need, budget, and timing.
- [Security](https://registrystack.org/security/): Access, accountability, and organizational responsibilities.
- [FAQ](https://registrystack.org/faq/): Product fit, adoption, evaluation, and licensing questions.
- [Contact](https://registrystack.org/contact/): Ask about a registry service, implementation, support or a proposal, or request access to a starting configuration.

## Technical evaluation

- [Base Registry Engine tutorial](https://docs.registrystack.org/tutorials/first-breg/): Create and update sample records, then test a refused request.
- [Evidence Gateway tutorial](https://docs.registrystack.org/tutorials/first-evidence-assertion/): Request a signed adult-status answer from a synthetic source and verify it.
- [Registry Casework overview](https://docs.registrystack.org/start/casework/): What runs where, how work reaches the inbox from a registry or a requesting service, and which guide to open next.
- [Documentation](https://docs.registrystack.org/): Maintained tutorials, technical contracts, release status, and operational guidance.
- [Source and releases](https://github.com/registrystack/registry-stack): Public source code and released software.

Website examples illustrate possible workflows; they are not live software demonstrations.
